subject: Request: Account-specific data-disposition variance & compensating controls (HealthPoint)
messages:
From: Amira Patel <compliance@healthpoint.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: sec-ops@healthpoint.com, legal@healthpoint.com
Date: Tue, 03 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: 45-day account-specific log retention variance and evidence

Hi Jonas,

We're finalizing our SIG/CAIQ mapping for the HealthPoint deployment and have a gap to close on data-disposition. Our policy requires a 45-day window for certain ephemeral application logs stored by vendors; Redwood's standard 90-day retention is acceptable generally, but our internal audit is asking for a documented exception and evidence that log exports and deletion are enforced to our 45-day requirement for the HealthPoint tenant only.

Specifically we need:
- A short description of the technical enforcement (how logs are identified and deleted per-tenant)
- Export process for data retained prior to deletion (S3 push or signed export)
- An audit trail demonstrating deletions (sample audit entries acceptable)
- Any compensating controls you can offer if you cannot shorten the retention period on the native platform (e.g., automated nightly export + key rotation + isolated storage)

Can you confirm feasibility and provide the requested artifacts (we can accept redacted samples for PII)? Deadline for our SIG submission is Oct 10.

Thanks,
Amira Patel
Sr. Compliance Manager
HealthPoint
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Patel <compliance@healthpoint.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Oct 2028 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: 45-day account-specific log retention variance and evidence

Amira —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: we can meet HealthPoint's requirement via an account-scoped disposition workflow and a nightly export, plus an audit trail. We typically retain raw inference logs for 90 days platform-wide, but we support account-level retention overrides when paired with compensating controls and an attestation process.

Next steps I propose:
1) I loop in Marissa (Security) and Neha (Legal) to validate controls and documentation.
2) We deliver a technical runbook and a redacted audit sample by Oct 6.
3) If HealthPoint signs a brief exception addendum (DocuSign), we operationalize the nightly export to your S3 and configure per-tenant deletion at 45 days.

Attachments I'm preparing: a 1-page compensating-controls proposal and an audit-log sample. If you can share the S3 destination details and any encryption requirements (KMS ARN), we can include that in the runbook.

Would you like a short call to walk through the mechanics? 30 minutes should be enough.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, Amira Patel <compliance@healthpoint.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 04 Oct 2028 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: 45-day account-specific log retention variance and evidence

Hi all,

Following Jon's note — quick security summary and proposed compensating controls we can operationalize for HealthPoint:

- Per-tenant retention override: Implemented as an account metadata flag that triggers the disposition pipeline. Deletions executed by the data-disposition job reference tenant_id and deletion markers; we only delete objects with matching tenant_id and a deletion timestamp older than the configured retention.

- Nightly export: We will push a compressed, encrypted bundle to HealthPoint's S3 bucket each night (AES-256, customer-managed KMS optional). Exports include only the log classes you approve (request/response traces, timestamp, trace_id) and will omit full prompts when PII is present; we can apply field-level redaction.

- Immutable audit trail: Each deletion action emits an audit record stored in our audit store (append-only), with: tenant_id, object_id(s), deletion_timestamp, operator-service, and export_manifest_id. We can provide a redacted audit sample (attached).

- Access controls: Export keys scoped to HealthPoint; exports written to a dedicated prefix with bucket policies that restrict list/delete to HealthPoint principals.

Limitations / notes:
- We cannot change the platform default retention for historical objects retroactively; exception applies moving forward once the addendum is signed and the flag is set.
- Requests asking for deletion sooner than 30 days require additional operational gating and a short rollout window to avoid data-loss for active debugging.

I attached a one-page controls proposal and a redacted audit-log sample. Jonas — if HealthPoint approves, we'll prepare an exception addendum and a short runbook for their security ops.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-compensating-controls-45d-export.pdf (application/pdf), audit-log-sample-2028Q3.txt (text/plain)
From: Amira Patel <compliance@healthpoint.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, sec-ops@healthpoint.com
Date: Thu, 05 Oct 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: 45-day account-specific log retention variance and evidence

Marissa / Jonas —

Thank you, this addresses most of the ask. A few clarifying points from our security team:
- The export manifest must include a checksum per file and a manifest signature (we can verify).
- We need to confirm redaction rules: specifically, request/response prompt text for PHI must be redacted by default.
- Can Redwood support a 7-day rolling quarantine window before deletion (i.e., export and then hold for 7 days in encrypted object storage visible only to HealthPoint) to allow us to pull for investigations? This would effectively make the retention 45 days before Redwood deletes, but HealthPoint would have an isolated 7-day accessible window where the exported data is retained only in our bucket.

If you can confirm these three items and produce the sample manifest with checksums, we'll route the requested exception through our Legal and sign the addendum.

Amira
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Patel <compliance@healthpoint.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 07 Oct 2028 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: 45-day account-specific log retention variance and evidence

Amira —

Confirming on Legal's side: we can proceed with the exception addendum. Responses to your three clarifications below:

1) Manifest + checksums: yes, we will include a signed JSON manifest containing file names, SHA-256 checksums, sizes, and an export_manifest_id. We'll produce a redacted sample manifest as part of the runbook.

2) Redaction rules: agreed — default behavior will mask prompt text that triggers PHI patterns; HealthPoint can provide a sample regex/pattern set and we'll add it to the export pipeline.

3) 7-day quarantine window in HealthPoint bucket: supported. Our nightly export will write to a dedicated encrypted prefix and set object lifecycle so only HealthPoint principals can access for 7 days; Redwood will not read those objects except in emergency with an approved access request. After 7 days HealthPoint may either archive or request full deletion; if no action, we will proceed with deleting platform-side copies per the 45-day disposition rule.

Next actions:
- I'll send a brief exception addendum (DocuSign) today for HealthPoint review (link included).
- Marissa, please attach the redacted manifest sample and runbook to the DocuSign packet.

Thanks — looking forward to finalizing.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: hp-sig-questionnaire-excerpt.pdf
Links: https://docsign.com/rw/HP-3421-exception, JIRA-RED-7892
